### D96 — The Wolfe ◄/► walk is freshness-guaranteed; quality curates only history (2026-07-10, S86c)
The completed-walk cap (`_OVERLAY_MAX=40`, top-N by §B quality) was taken across the WHOLE
history, so on a long series a freshly confirmed wave could lose to decades-old high-Q waves and
become invisible — exactly how Ramana's textbook TCS Jun-2026 falling wedge (Q15.0, §A all-pass,
leg ratio 0.937) vanished: TCS has 261 confirmed waves since 2004 and the #40 quality cutoff is
Q17.33. Decision: `wolfe._FRESH_KEEP_BARS = 250` — every CONFIRMED wave whose point 5 printed
within the last trading year enters the walk regardless of Q; the walk still sorts newest-first.
WHY a decision: the walk's job is reading CURRENT structure — the quality cut exists only to
curate the historical tail, and must never gate recency. §A geometry, §B scoring and the
winner-profile scanner are untouched. (TCS walk 37→53; the missed wave now sits at 2/53.)

### D95 — Corporate-action adjustment is TAPE-PRIMARY with a tolerance gate; the D36 prev_close layer is measured-dead (2026-07-10, S86b)
The S85e adjust-vs-tape reconciliation FALSIFIED D36's core assumption: NSE does NOT write the
adjusted prior close into bhav `prev_close` on ex-dates (measured across every era 2004→2026;
r_pc = 1.0 on all sampled ex-dates incl. IPCALAB 2022) — the "primary" detector never fired once,
and every adjustment ever made came from the ≥30 % close-jump fallback alone. Actions moving
3–30 % (a 1:3 bonus ≈ −25 %) were therefore invisible: **112 event-groups / 92 symbols** carried
mixed price scales in 52w-high / RS / drift / key_price. Decision: the adjustment doctrine is now
**tape-primary** — `corp_actions.price_ratios` (exact ex-date + ratio; same-day events compound)
drives `adjust.adjustment_factors(events=)`, **tolerance-gated ±18 %** against the observed ex-day
move so a mis-parsed/mis-dated tape row can never corrupt a series (77 TAPE_SUSPECTs — reversed
bonus-subject conventions, split-across-rows compounds — are refused and flagged, inference stands).
`events=None` stays byte-identical legacy. The prev_close layer is KEPT but documented dead. WHY a
decision: every consumer of adjusted prices must eventually pass the tape (`signals.py` wired now;
mep/cpr/stock_rs/mtf/wolfe/ignition_backtest/cockpit/rrg_view/dashboard-inline = the recorded
adoption wave), and no new consumer may ship inference-only. Permanent audit: `corp_actions
--reconcile`; nightly guard: `chk_action_tape_agreement`.

### D82 — XBRL Phase 2: banks map by TAG-detection into Screener bank conventions, quarterly-only; unmappable definitional cohorts stay gate-failed rather than guessed; long writers may never starve startup (2026-07-02, session 75)
Three linked decisions, all evidence-driven (live instances + Screener DB reconciliation, `docs/fundamentals-xbrl-migration.md` § Phase-2 evidence):
- **(a) Bank/NBFC mapper.** Bank instances are detected by TAGS (`InterestEarned` present), never listing flags (HDFCBANK's own listing says `bank="N"`). Extraction (`extract_bank_for`) reproduces Screener's bank conventions to the rupee — `Revenue=InterestEarned`, `Expenses=OperatingExpenses+Provisions`, `Financing Profit=Rev−Int−Exp`, structural `PBT/NP` INCLUDING ExceptionalItems + associates (tagged PBT/PAT are unreliable — filers stuff MI into ExceptionalItems). Reconcile: Revenue/FP 100%, NP 100% for ICICIBANK+SBIN (6 qtrs). **Quarterly only** — Screener bank ANNUALS come from annual reports (separate depreciation line the results-XBRL lacks); Phase 3 owns them. Bank gate core = Revenue/Net Profit/Financing Profit. Verdicts: **ICICIBANK PASS · SBIN PASS · HDFCBANK FAIL by design** (chronic MI-in-ExceptionalItems misfiling, admitted in its own notes — refusal > guessing).
- **(b) Definitional mappers dissolved by evidence, not built on speculation.** ITC excise-gross Sales is NOT mappable (the instance carries no excise fact — it hides untagged in OtherExpenses) → stays gate-failed until Phase-3 series replacement. LT NCI netting NOT needed (Screener stores PAT incl NCI = `ProfitLossForPeriod`, matches exactly). LT other-op-income OP: identity reproduces exactly on current quarters — no mapper. New `--regate` CLI re-arbitrates cached gate verdicts after any mapper change; `--selftest` guards the bank identity synthetically.
- **(c) DB startup is writer-tolerant (the outage root-fix pair).** Companion to `a4f1c21` (ingest commits PER FILING — the write lock never spans a network fetch): `db._init` now catches a locked/busy schema-init and, when the schema already exists from a prior boot, STARTS SERVING + retries the idempotent DDL in a background thread (fresh DB still fails hard). Verified live: hermes-api restarted cleanly WHILE the insider backfill was writing — the exact 2026-07-02 outage scenario. `busy_timeout` must stay < systemd `TimeoutStartSec` (90s); tolerance, not timeout, is the fix.

### D78 — Fundamentals go primary-source: NSE-XBRL forward ingest with a per-symbol series-continuity gate; Screener history frozen, never overwritten (2026-07-02, session 73)
The Guardrail-#8 remediation, designed against a risk-governance + data-product panel memo and live endpoint probes. **Source:** NSE financial-results XBRL, TWO APIs split by the Apr-2025 SEBI Integrated-Filing regime change — legacy `corporates-financial-results` (through Apr-2025 + late old-period filers; symbol+date-range combined returns 0 rows, filter client-side) and `integrated-filing-results` (thin listing → parse-first-classify from the instance's own meta tags; path recovered from NSE's `corporate-filings.js`). **Facts:** absolute INR (÷1e7 = ₹ cr) in the shared `in-bse-fin` taxonomy; context IDs encode the results-table COLUMN (`OneD` quarter / `FourD` FY / `OneI` instant) and filers stamp degenerate dates into `FourD`, so named contexts are primary. **PIT:** `knowable_at` = exchange broadcast datetime via `provenance.observe`; restatement = last-filed value wins, earliest knowable preserved. **The gate (the design's heart):** reconciliation proved Screener-era rows use restated/netted definitions for SOME symbols (ITC excise-gross Sales +13%, ULTRACEMCO merger-restated PAT, LT other-operating-income OP −20%, EPS restated across bonuses — RELIANCE exactly 2×), so blind appending would corrupt cross-boundary CAGRs; ingest therefore writes a symbol only after its recent historical filings MATCH the Screener series on the rupee core (Sales/Net Profit/OP, 2%, `fundamentals_xbrl_gate` cached; no-overlap auto-pass; verified live: RELIANCE/TCS pass 18/18, ITC fails as predicted). Every row carries `source` (`NSE-XBRL-CONSO`/`-SA`; NULL = Screener era); nil is NEVER coerced to zero (one documented exception: a filed balance sheet with no borrowings tags = debt-free 0.0); a period whose whole rupee core is exactly 0 is a blank column, rejected (IL&FSTRANS FY19 late filing — which also proved the PIT path: period 2019-03-31, report_date 2026-07-01). Full design + reconciliation evidence: `docs/fundamentals-xbrl-migration.md`. Consumers unchanged (same table/metric names). Phase 2 = definitional mappers + banks + shareholding; Phase 3 = historical backfill, then delete `screener.py`.

### D76 — Data-roadmap ROI: build C (capital-allocation) → A (insider/promoter) → B (credit ratings); the winner is chosen by NIFTY regime-fit, not popularity (2026-07-02, session 63)
Ramana had a ChatGPT brainstorm producing a 40-row "data wishlist"; most of it is already built here. - **A. Insider/promoter/pledge events** — the flagship first *new* feed. Highest orthogonality, densest in the smallcap tail where alpha migrated, carries both conviction (open-market buys) and distress (pledge/selling). Every tail name has a promoter who files under A; most are unrated so B is blind exactly there. Scoring objective = `(decision-impact × PIT-confidence × source-reliability × orthogonality) / (effort × false-positive-cleanup)`. Brief: `docs/DATASET-RESEARCH-BRIEF.md`. **C SHIPPED** (`src/automation/capital_allocation.py`, `capital_allocation_scores` table). **A LIVE** (`src/automation/insider_events.py`, `insider_events` table — classifier + PIT aggregation + **live NSE `corporates-pit` fetcher, validated: 4,834 events ingested, 3 taxonomy fixes from real data**). **B LIVE** (`src/automation/credit_ratings.py`, `credit_rating_events` — parser + ordinal ladder + action classifier + linkage; **validated: 2,738 events, 4 real-data fixes: content-hash uid, notch-suffix regex, fresh-default-only, whole-token grade match (prose like "BANK"→B was flagging AAA issuers below-IG)**). ### D73 — The committed repo is self-sufficient: the v2-surfaces hook lives in committed `main.py` (a clean clone + deploy renders the full v2 site, no post-deploy script needed) (2026-06-29, session 50)

(1) `src/main.py` now ends with the canonical `# === v2 surfaces hook (durable) ===` block (defensive `try/except` around `v2_surfaces.wire(app)`) — **byte-identical to what `wire_v2_surfaces.py` appends**, so the operational script is now a clean **NO-OP** against the committed tree (it still works as the post-clobber re-applier; it just has nothing to do on a fresh clone). The change is **additive + reversible** (delete the hook block to revert; the routers fall back to unmounted) and **idempotent + defensive** (every step inside `wire()` is `try/except`, the nav install is sentinel-guarded, routers skip if already present). **Verify (local):** `python -m src.web.v2_surfaces` selftest green (now also asserts every `_ROUTER_SPECS` router is actually mounted by `wire()`); `from src.main import app` boots with all 9 v2 routes present + zero duplicate `/dash` registrations; `python scripts/wire_v2_surfaces.py .` reports **"NO-OP: clean hook already present."** Page-render liveness of the data-dependent pages (growth/testing read `research.db`) is verified on the VPS by `scripts/regression_sweep.sh` (both already in its ROUTES set). ### D70 — Wolfe detector: the SELL setup is an ascending wedge (L,H,L,H), not the H,L,H,L mirror — fixes the wave/pivot-selection defect (2026-06-24, session 40)
The live Wolfe overlay drew a different wave than Ramana draws in Fyers: on PARAS he draws a **rising** wave whose strong Fib zone (~1226) sits **above** (he sells the overshoot), but the detector showed a **bear with a downward ~807 zone**. Root cause, found by a 4-seat expert panel (quant·viz·skeptic·Ramana-proxy) + an empirical probe: the detector's `_classify` only admitted L,H,L,H with *descending* lows (BULL) or H,L,H,L with *ascending* highs (BEAR), so it **could not emit Ramana's pivots at all** (his are an ASCENDING L,H,L,H, 3>1 & 4>2) — even with symmetry widened. The Fib FORMULA was already right (`fib_zones` reproduces his 1226.2 = 2.618∩2.618 to the decimal); only wave SELECTION was wrong. **The anchor (panel-decided):** the two thrust legs 1→2 & 3→4 point TOWARD point 5 (their standard-Fib-extension confluence is the point-5 zone — literally his method). So: **BEAR/SELL = ascending wedge** (L,H,L,H, lows & highs rise, legs up, point 5 = the upper overshoot of the **2-4 rail** = the Fib-confluence zone, reverse DOWN) — this is PARAS, painted RED. **BULL/BUY = descending wedge — UNCHANGED** (kept exactly as Ramana's 2026-06-23 correction; the skeptic seat vetoed relabeling it H,L,H,L-descending, which would resurrect the "no-upside-EPA" labelling he retracted). **H,L,H,L decompositions dropped** (legs point away from 5 → the bogus 807-side zone). **Symmetry tol widened 0.6→0.5** (PARAS legs = 0.583). **Point-5 zone unified on the Fib confluence** (strongest overlap on the overshoot side; symmetry projection only as fallback) so `/dash/wolfe` and the candle overlay agree. **Viz:** overlay de-cluttered — only structure + EPA + the single strongest zone by default; the 2×13 Fib grids, the 1-3 rail, and weaker zones hidden behind a snippet-injected "grid" toggle; `overlay_for` now returns ALL waves best-first + a `‹ › / near` selector (all controls injected by the snippet → **dashboard.py / main.py untouched**). **Edge probe (#4, PIT-honest):** v1 looked spectacular (+7%/78%) but was **repaint look-ahead** (a zigzag point 5 is only confirmed after price already reversed ~k·ATR); entering at the *confirmation bar* instead, the edge **vanishes** (ALL Wolfe +0.06%/50%pos, ≈−0.8pp vs baseline) — even the tight-symmetry / HIGH-tier subsets show nothing. So the mechanical lens earns **NO buy/sell verdict** → stays **DESCRIPTIVE-ONLY** (doctrine upheld; this doesn't test his discretionary zone-anticipation + fusion method). Files (isolated, committed): `src/automation/wolfe.py`, `src/web/wolfe_view.py`, `src/web/wolfe_overlay.py`, `research/wolfe_waves/selftest.py`, `docs/wolfe-*.md`. Deployed to VPS (scp+restart, LF; backups `*.bak-0624fix`); selftest green; PARAS now reads ascending-wedge BEARs with upward zones. Open: **#B1** reconcile the BUY/descending Wolfe with the Fib-method anchor against a real buy drawing; exact-pivot match needs fractal/click-two-swings (his hand pivots aren't strict zigzag — P3>P2). Full panel record + rationale in `docs/wolfe-NEXT-SESSION.md` §7.

### D69 — Leverage / inverse derivative indexes get NO RS read (their ratio is mechanical, not informational) (2026-06-24, session 38)
Ramana flagged that **Nifty 50 TR 2x Leverage** was getting the full RRG / RS treatment on its index page. It shouldn't: a leveraged/inverse index's ratio vs the broad market is MECHANICAL — a 2x index just scales the market (it pins to an extreme "leading" in any uptrend, flips to "lagging" in a downtrend), an inverse is a mirrored one, and the **TR** variants add a dividend-reinvestment drift measured against the **PR** Nifty 500 benchmark, so the RS line trends up perpetually regardless of real strength. The framework reads it as a permanent extreme — noise, and exactly the "is this data authentic?" failure the brand can't afford. It was already kept off the `/dash/rrg` MAP (curated to `REAL_SECTORS`) but its own detail page + `/dash/ratio` still rendered the misleading mini-RRG. **Decision:** extend the D67 `gets_rs` gate to ALSO exclude leverage/inverse derivatives — new `RS_EXCLUDE_TOKENS = ("LEVERAGE", "INVERSE")`, matched as case-insensitive substrings (`gets_rs = nameU not in BROAD_MARKET_PROXIES and not any(tok in nameU for tok in RS_EXCLUDE_TOKENS)`). They now carry `broad_benchmark=NULL` → `is_broad=True` → price-only detail page (return-spread table, no mini-RRG), and `/dash/ratio` shows "no ratio series." Tokens are **LEVERAGE / INVERSE only — deliberately NOT "TR"/"PR"**, which would wrongly hit "Infrastructure" etc. (verified 10/10: the 4 leverage/inverse variants + the broad proxies are out; Infrastructure / Alpha / Smallcap-250 / Defence / Bank stay RS-eligible). `index_signals.py` only (clean file); rides the D67 deploy. **Deploy caveat:** the engine stops COMPUTING their ratios, but a one-time `DELETE FROM ratio_rows / rs_extras / capture_signals / rs_band WHERE numerator LIKE '%Leverage%' OR LIKE '%Inverse%'` is needed on the VPS to clear any PRE-existing rows (the backfill is INSERT-OR-REPLACE, never deletes — so a stale `rs_extras` row would still surface a depth panel). **Open:** pure 1x-TR indexes (if any in the feed) keep the PR-vs-TR drift but aren't caught by these tokens — revisit with the live index list (couldn't enumerate now: VPS down, local DB empty). Factor indexes (Alpha / Momentum / Low-Vol) deliberately KEPT — their RS is meaningful. Full arc → Session 38.

### D145 — A headless GLM-5.2 code reviewer on the VPS — REPORT-ONLY, isolated from the production Anthropic client (2026-06-24, session 39; renumbered from D68 → D145 in S194c to heal the collision with the rotation-vocabulary D68 below — the GLM decision was the later claimant, session 39 vs 38)
Ramana asked to "install ZCode on the VPS and create a project that continuously reviews our code and fixes it with the free package of GLM 5.2." Two facts reshaped the literal request: (1) **ZCode is a desktop GUI app** (Z.ai's `.dmg`/desktop installer — no headless/CLI/daemon mode per its docs), so it cannot run on a headless VPS at all; (2) auto-**fixing** live code on a box that runs the bot/API/scoring AND whose git tree is chronically dirty + shared by parallel sessions is unsafe. After surfacing both, Ramana chose: **report-only** (never edits code), **headless CLI on the VPS**, and **whole repo may be sent** to Z.ai (he accepts the IP exposure of the free tier). **Decision:** build a Hermes-idiomatic scheduled job — `src/automation/code_review.py` + a nightly `hermes-code-review.{service,timer}` — that sends a slice of the source to GLM-5.2 via Z.ai's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (`https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic`, model `glm-5.2`), writes a dated report to `data/code_reviews/`, and pushes a summary to the owner's Telegram DM. **WHY the key architectural choices:** (a) **own isolated Anthropic client** — the reviewer constructs `Anthropic(api_key=GLM_API_KEY, base_url=GLM_BASE_URL)` explicitly and reads config from its OWN `GLM_*` env vars, NOT `src.core.llm.client()` and NOT a global `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`. Setting `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` globally on the VPS would silently redirect the **production bot's real Anthropic traffic** to Z.ai — must never happen. (b) **report-only** — the VPS deploy reality (dirty tree, parallel sessions) makes any auto-edit a collision/again-st-prod risk; findings go to a human. (c) **deploy is purely additive** — new files only (no edit to the shared, possibly-divergent VPS `settings.py`); installer writes its 2 units via heredoc (LF-safe) and does NOT `git pull`. (d) **cost** — this path never touches Anthropic (₹0 to the ~₹300/mo budget); GLM-5.2's free quota is finite + time-limited, so each run is byte/file-capped and the schedule is nightly (auto mode: review the working-tree diff if dirty, else a rotating full-repo sweep). **State:** built + state-documented this session; **NOT yet deployed** (sandbox can't reach the VPS on :22) and **needs a Z.ai `GLM_API_KEY`** in `/opt/hermes/.env` before it does anything — until then it cleanly no-ops. Deploy run-book in § Session log → Session 39.

### D68 — One rotation vocabulary everywhere: the single-element quads become true mini-RRGs (RS-Ratio × RS-Momentum + JdK labels + tail) (2026-06-24, session 38)
Ramana flagged a second inconsistency on the index page: the abs×rel quadrant used **LEADER / DEFENSIVE / LAGGARD / LAZY-LAGGARD** on *3m-return × 3m-RS-slope* axes, while the RS-depth panel right below it (and the full `/dash/rrg`) used the JdK **Leading / Weakening / Lagging / Improving** on *RS-Ratio × RS-Momentum* axes. Two rotation languages on one page — and worse, they could DISAGREE (the return×slope quad could read "leader" while the depth panel read "weakening", because the axes differ). **Decision:** the JdK vocabulary is the canonical rotation language EVERYWHERE; the single-element quads are converted to true mini-RRGs that share the EXACT axes, quadrant geometry, ~100 normalisation, colours (`rrg_view.QCOLOR`), and `rrg.quadrant()` mapping as the full RRG — so the mini-quad, the depth panel, and `/dash/rrg` can never disagree again. **Implementation:** new ISOLATED module **`src/web/mini_rrg.py`** — `mini_rrg_card(full_tail, den, …)`, a pure renderer fed by `rrg.tail(num, den, n, conn)` (the same on-read tail engine the stock-RRG page uses). Both bespoke quads now call it: `cockpit.render_index_detail` (the live index page) and `dashboard` `/dash/ratio`. Each draws the index's RS-Ratio × RS-Momentum **journey** as a fading comet tail into today's dot (the tail Ramana asked for), coloured by the live quadrant. The old return×slope quads — incl. the brief return-slope tail added earlier this session — are removed. The single-stock RRG (`rrg_view._stock_rrg_page`) was already canonical → untouched. **Scope of "everywhere" (verified):** only those 2 quads used the old vocab — `DEFENSIVE` / `LAZY LAGGARD` existed only there; `cockpit.py:_index_verdict`'s "DEFENSIVE / RELATIVE WINNER" is a different abs×rel VERDICT headline (not a quadrant) and is left as-is. Rides the same uncommitted `cockpit.py` / `dashboard.py` deploy as D67 and needs nothing extra: the tail reads `ratio_rows`, which the D67 backfill already populates for the size indexes (sectors already have it). Full arc in § Session log → Session 38.

### D67 — Cap-segment size indexes get the FULL RS-vs-broad read (Smallcap 250 ≡ a sector on its detail page) (2026-06-24, session 38)
Ramana flagged that `/dash/index?idx=Nifty Smallcap 250` showed only a bare "Relative strength vs Nifty 500" return-spread **table**, while a sector (Nifty India Defence) showed the whole RS apparatus — RS-ratio chart + RRG quadrant + RS-depth (RSI-of-RS / Mansfield) + capture + RS support/resistance — **under the same heading**. Same words, different content = a credibility / data-authenticity problem. **Root cause (traced, not guessed):** `index_signals.compute_for_date` gated the entire ratio engine on `if not is_size_based:` and forced `broad_benchmark=NULL` for every name in `SIZE_BASED_INDEX_NAMES`. That null cascades — no `ratio_rows`, and because `rs_extras` (rrg.py) / `capture_signals` / `rsband` ALL iterate `SELECT DISTINCT numerator FROM ratio_rows`, no RRG / Mansfield / RSI-of-RS / capture / band either; then on the page `is_broad = (bb is None)` routes size indexes to the bare-table branch. The code's stated rationale ("size indexes have no single ratio-line series") was **false** — `Smallcap 250 ÷ Nifty 500` is the canonical small-cap-leadership line; the rotation engine was simply built sector-first and bucketed ALL size indexes as "broad," sweeping the useful cap segments in with the degenerate aggregates. **Decision:** narrow the exclusion from "all size indexes" to **only the aggregate broad-market proxies** — new set `BROAD_MARKET_PROXIES = {Nifty 100, Nifty 200, Nifty 500, Nifty Total Market}`, where a ratio vs Nifty 500 genuinely IS near-circular. Gate becomes `gets_rs = name.upper() not in BROAD_MARKET_PROXIES`; it computes the ratio + sets `broad_benchmark='Nifty 500'` for the **11 admitted cap segments** (Nifty 50, Next 50, Midcap 50/100/150, Smallcap 50/100/250, Microcap 250, Largemidcap 250, Midsmallcap 400). Everything downstream lights up automatically off `ratio_rows` — **zero edits to rrg.py / capture.py / rsband.py** — and the detail page's existing `if not is_broad` branch renders the full RS section for them with no view rewrite. **Why this doesn't pollute sector views:** sector rotation / leaderboards / the RRG scatter / the band leaderboard all curate to `dashboard.REAL_SECTORS` (NOT `bb IS NOT NULL`), so the admitted size indexes never show up as "sectors." The ONE place `bb` doubled as the grouping flag — the live markets-bundle filter in `cockpit.render_markets` — was switched to group by `SIZE_BASED_INDEX_NAMES` membership, so Smallcap 250 stays under "Broad / size", not "Sectoral." **Files:** `index_signals.py` (engine) + `cockpit.py` (one grouping line). **Requires** a one-time `index_signals --backfill` on the VPS to populate `ratio_rows` history for the 11 names, then the nightly rs_extras / capture / band passes fill the rest. `Nifty 100/200` excluded deliberately (≈ Nifty 500); trivial to admit later. Full arc in § Session log → Session 38.

### D66 — Point-in-time fundamentals → backtestable patearn score; the score is a RISK FILTER, returns come from accumulation (2026-06-23, session 37)
The 24-year fundamentals archive already existed (`research.db.fundamentals_history`, 1,983 syms × 2002–2026, point-in-time via `report_date`) — so the work was INTEGRATION, not collection. Built **`src/automation/fundamentals_asof.py`** — a point-in-time reader returning the exact dict `scoring.score_fundamentals` consumes (drop-in, no scorer rewrite) plus real trend keys; no-look-ahead proven at the +90d/+50d report lag. **`scoring.py` upgraded** — 7 data-starved patterns (P1 ROCE trend, P2/P10 OPM trend, P5 interest coverage, P9 profit acceleration, P12 debtor days, P13 cash-conversion cycle, P6 promoter-rising) now use REAL verified signals when the trend keys are present, else fall back to the old proxy — so the LIVE Telegram path (snapshot dict, no trend keys) is byte-for-byte unchanged (regression-safe). **`research/explosive_moves/fund_panel.py`** — survivorship-aware PIT panel (patearn score as-of every monthly rebalance ⨝ forward 1/3/6/12m returns; a delisted name realizes its return-to-last-price instead of dropping out); ₹5cr liquid universe; `research.db.fund_panel` (51,652 rows). **`research/explosive_moves/combo_test.py`** — joins `fund_panel ⨝ ml_panel` via a `combined_panel` VIEW (tables kept SEPARATE; view = saved join, no copied data). **`src/automation/shareholding_history.py`** — quarterly promoter/FII/DII/public from Screener's shareholding section → `research.db.shareholding_history` (separate table; ~12q/~3y depth; NO pledge — needs BSE); wired into `fundamentals_asof` (P6/P8 real for 2023+). **FINDINGS (survivorship-aware backtest; descriptive — overlapping monthly obs, not significance-tested):** (1) the patearn fundamental score is a **RISK FILTER, not a return ranker** — blow-up rate (>50% loss/12m) falls monotonically by tier (T2 0% → T3 2% → T4 4% → DISQ 5%) while median return is ~flat (NS long-short ≈ 0). (2) **Returns come from accumulation/RS** — top-tercile 3m delivery-drift ≈ 11% median 12m vs ~5% weak. (3) **Sweet spot = strong accumulation + good fundamentals** (≈11% median / 60% hit / **2%** blow-up). (4) **T1 never forms** (NS caps ~63) because P3/P7/P11/P14 + pledge stay estimated — and P11 (VCP) + P14 (volume) are exactly what `ml_panel`/bhav already hold, so a unified T1-capable score = fold the technical-confirmation patterns into the scorer. **Doctrine impact:** quantitatively confirms D62 (DVPT/accumulation = the signal; fundamentals = the quality/risk gate). **Deploy:** files scp'd to VPS; research runs under `.venv-research` (numpy); note `db.py` is stdlib-only so `scoring` imports with no heavy deps. Full arc in § Session log → Session 37.

### D65 — MEP is headlined as a smoothed, hysteresis-banded PHASE, not the daily score (2026-06-22, session 35)
The daily `mep_score` flips state ~3 days in 4 (RELIANCE 50 changes / 70 rows) because 3 of its 4 terms are essentially today's bar — a pressure **oscillator**, not the accumulation→consolidation→distribution **regime** it was framed as. **Decision:** store + headline a **PHASE** — `mep_score_smooth` (rolling mean of the daily score over **15** trading rows) banded through a **hysteresis ladder** (asymmetric enter/exit deadbands) into `mep_state_smooth`. The daily score is kept underneath everywhere (data-first). **Why window 15, not the "~10" first sketched:** a VPS grid-search showed 15 is the *smallest* window that puts every reference stock **single-digit** transitions/70 (avg 5.7, max 8 — an 8.5× cut from 48.8); win10–14 leave choppy range-bound large-caps (SBIN/WIPRO) at 10–13. Bands calibrated to the real smoothed-score spread (σ≈0.43) so STRONG is the selective ~10% tail and NEUTRAL/consolidation is the plurality. **Still descriptor-only (D62)** — the phase, however clean, does not rank/pick. Full design + calibration: `docs/mep-strategy-design.md` §9; the multi-lens decode preserved in §10.

### D64 — RRG rotation map + RS-depth (RSI-of-RS / Mansfield) + down-capture + constituent drill-down (2026-06-22)
Ramana asked to deepen relative strength and make rotation *visual + drillable*. Decisions:
- **JdK normalisation (~100)** for RS-Ratio (x) and RS-Momentum (y) so every sector/stock is comparable on one quadrant chart (kills the IT-1.19 vs Bank-2.0 magnitude problem).
- **RSI-of-RS** = Wilder RSI on the RS *ratio line* (NOT the price); **Mansfield RS** = RS ÷ its own long MA (zero-centred, doesn't saturate like RSI). Both for turns/divergence at extremes, never as a standalone trend signal. **RS-Momentum** (unbounded) drives the map.
- **Nifty 500 = primary benchmark; Nifty 50 = the cap-tilt / breadth divergence lens** (both already computed).
- **Down-capture** (`capture.py`): "accumulate what falls LESS than the Nifty (<1), avoid what falls faster" — regime-gate the "accumulate" framing; the *change* in down-capture is the real alpha.
- **Constituent drill-down** defaults to **vs the sector** (spreads participants by intra-sector strength) with a `vs=broad` (Nifty 500) toggle.
- **Placement (financial/UI-UX/architect 3-lens):** RRG is a view INSIDE Markets — the **Sectors page is the home** (map overview on top + RS table below), plus a full-screen `/dash/rrg`; **NOT a 6th nav tab**. Funnel: Markets → Sectors[map+table] → drill to constituents → click a stock.
- **Isolation:** built as new modules (`rrg.py`/`capture.py`/`rrg_view.py` + a systemd drop-in), mounted 1-line in `main.py`, so it never edits the parallel-contended `dashboard.py`/`cockpit.py`; the drill lives entirely in `/dash/rrg`. Distinct from the parallel **weather rotation** (`/dash/rotation`, phase buckets) — RRG is the continuous scatter; complementary, link don't compete. Run-book + autonomous self-prompt: `docs/rrg-rotation-NEXT-SESSION.md`.

### D63 — Theme tags: a MULTI-LABEL thematic layer, deterministic-seed-first, AI-proposes/Ramana-approves (2026-06-22, session 33)
NEW classification layer (Ramana's locked spec). **Why a new layer at all:** `primary_sector` is single-label; index membership is the natural multi-label seed but isn't surfaced as a browsable thematic lens. Themes give the multi-label view (RELIANCE → Energy + Oil & Gas + Infrastructure + Commodities) + a place for cross-cutting ideas no index captures (Industrialization-proxy, Make-in-India, …). **Decisions:** (1) **ADDITIVE, never replaces** — a sibling to sector/index; `company_tags` is a separate table; `primary_sector`/`stock_index_membership` untouched; sacred pages untouched. (2) **Three provenance tiers** — `index` (deterministic fact from a thematic index, approved=1), `ai` (LLM-proposed, approved=0, shown "proposed"), `ramana` (hand-approved/added, approved=1); PK `(symbol, tag, source)` so a tag can hold both a fact and a human provenance; reads dedupe by tag (DISTINCT). (3) **Vocabulary = a code constant** (`THEME_VOCAB` in `theme_tags.py`) — the single source of truth, version-controlled, extendable by editing the module; 19 deterministic (seeded 1:1/union from the NSE thematic indices) + 6 cross-cutting (empty until AI/manual). The themes page shows the FULL taxonomy incl. empty ones (honest "awaiting"). (4) **Deterministic-FIRST given reality:** `fundamentals` has NO business descriptions and covers only ~55 names, so the Haiku-from-descriptions layer can't run yet — the **deterministic index seed is the day-one product** (355 tags live, genuinely multi-label), and the AI layer is **gated** on a `company_about` corpus (now harvested best-effort by `screener.fetch_company`). (5) **Cost:** the proposer routes through `llm_router.call_classifier` (Gemini Flash → Haiku fallback per doctrine D20), **never Sonnet**, ≤ quarterly — this is the doctrine-correct reading of the run-book's "Haiku proposes" shorthand (theme-tagging is a classification task). (6) **Index-derived themes deliberately overlap sector** — the value is the multi-label set (multi-index membership → several tags), not novelty vs `primary_sector`. (7) **Refresh:** a self-contained weekly `hermes-theme-seed.timer` reseeds the deterministic layer from current membership (idempotent; never touches ai/ramana). Surfaces: stock-page chips · `/dash/themes` + `/dash/theme?tag=` · screener `g-themes` column + filter · index participants Themes column + the shared `_participants_table` · `/dash/tags-review`. (8) **ISOLATION — BINDING (Ramana, 2026-06-22):** the theme layer is STRICTLY for tags and must NEVER pollute or alter the standard indices or sectors. It WRITES only `company_tags` + `company_about` (verified: zero writes to `stock_index_membership`/`index_signals`/`index_rows`/`ratio_rows`/`primary_sector`/`stock_signals`); the seeder only READS membership to derive; sector/index analytics compute purely from the standard tables — tags are an additive display layer beside them. Corpus backfills must write `company_about` only (a description-only fetch), NOT refresh `fundamentals` as a side effect. Full build in § Session log → Session 33.

### D62 — DVPT reframed: a counterparty-fragmentation gauge, NOT a leading smart-money signal → demoted to confirmation/character layer (2026-06-22)
Ramana challenged the DVPT premise on first principles; the analysis confirmed it and reconciled the docs. **Mechanics:** DVPT = delivery value ÷ `num_trades` (day's *total* trades); a trade prints per order match, so `num_trades` collapses only when BOTH sides are concentrated. The target case — one informed buyer absorbing fragmented retail supply — generates many matches → high trade count → low, retail-looking DVPT (invisible). DVPT spikes only when the counterparty is ALSO concentrated = a block/bulk transfer, **already disclosed with client names**. So **DVPT reads the counterparty's fragmentation, not the accumulator's conviction**; modern execution (VWAP/iceberg) fragments on purpose → DVPT selects against sophistication; it is side-blind (the D43 character gate's *price* input does the real directional work); and post-₹-floor-removal a thin name's high DVPT can be one lumpy print. **Matches D56's data verdict** ("no stealth accumulation footprint before +10% moves in the EOD aggregate"; whale-among-minnows REFUTED). **Decision:** DVPT/delivery is no longer positioned as a *leading* signal or a standalone picking engine; it survives as a **confirmation/character layer** on price (move-is-paid-for / divergence / within-stock-relative), and the WHO-is-transacting decode moves to the **named-flow channel** (`deals.py`: bulk/block + FII/DII, + F&O OI when located). Full reconciliation in `docs/dvpt-picking-strategy-design.md` § 0 (original v0.1 thesis kept for history). Multi-lens accumulation/distribution decode (orthogonal equations) explored same day — to be documented when it firms up.

### D61 — Rank & compare on MEASURABLE items only; qualitative content is INFORMATION (2026-06-22, applies to ALL strategies)
Ramana's ruling: a strategy's **score and cross-stock comparison must rest only on objective, reproducible, measurable inputs.** Interpretive/LLM content — tone, "credibility feel", under/over/concealed opinions, the 0–100 behaviour axes — is **information** (a sentence + at most a couple of coarse attributes shown beside the verdict), **never a ranking input**. The bar is reproducibility + ground-truthability. DVPT/RS/CPR/pt14 already comply (they rank on computed numbers); **CCI was the exception** (it blended LLM 0–100 credibility/transparency/tone into the composite) → **FIXED:** `concall_scores.py` now ranks on `guidance_accuracy` (kept-promise hit-rate), `quantification_rate` (% of forward statements that are *falsifiable numbers* — the deterministic "transparency", computed from `claim_text` via `cci_normalize.classify_commitment`; **replaces** the LLM transparency score), the **forensic veto** (pledge/auditor/pt14), and **deterministic deterioration** (disclosure-diff flags only). The 10 behaviour axes are still stored + shown as an **"AI read — not ranked"**. An **unproven** name (no settled promises) is capped below A/A+. Verified live: IDEA quantification 94.4% vs RELIANCE 76.9% (both unproven → capped B). **General rule going forward: if an attribute can't be measured reproducibly, it informs but does not rank.**

### D60 — Concall Intelligence (CCI): a management-credibility / guidance-accuracy strategy + the debate inversion (2026-06-21/22)
NEW strategy — the qualitative forward layer D56 pointed to. Read Indian earnings concalls (Screener "Concalls" section → BSE transcript PDFs, free, `pypdf`, no OCR), capture every management promise → grade it against what actually landed in the next result/call → compound into a per-company **credibility score + rank** + a **deterioration (avoid) tape**. **9 tables:** concalls, concall_results, concall_ebitda_watch, concall_guidance (promise ledger / capex follow-through), concall_expectations_vs_actual (in-line/understated/overstated/CONCEALED + headwind-adjusted), concall_behavior (credibility/transparency/courage/… 0–100), concall_redflags, concall_scores, concall_coverage (survivorship spine). One-time **Gemini** extraction per transcript (cached, `json_mode`); **zero-LLM scoring**; deep nuance → claude.ai. An **8-lens adversarial debate** (`docs/concall-intelligence-debate.md`) caught a real flaw — scoring credibility from the suspect's own testimony ranks the best-spoken frauds highest — so the scorer was **INVERTED**: forensic **VETO first** (promoter pledge ≥20% + pt14 hard-disqualifiers, cash-flow vetoes sector-suppressed for fin/heavy-capex) → tier D/AVOID; **resolved track-record primary**; **UNPROVEN ceiling** (no A/A+ without resolved promises); deterioration penalty; tone only as per-speaker deviation; **build-failing price↔credibility firewall**. **Engine B (price-mispricing) DEFERRED.** Sequence (supersedes design §9): cheap **falsification gates BEFORE scale** → merge into pt14 if no incremental alpha over quality+PEAD. **Constraint:** Gemini free tier = 20 req/day → historical backfill via **claude.ai (free)** or paid Gemini. **Status (session 29):** P1–P7 **BUILT + DEPLOYED** (VPS, scp + hermes-api restart): full backend chain (results→settle→diff→score) + refinements (lender-revenue capture, EBITDA-suppressed-for-financials, implied-growth settlement, `--oldest` backfill order) + **P5 UI** (per-stock CCI **dossier** on `/dash/stock`, `credibility · cci` **screener column-group**, **Pat** credibility/deterioration NL flows) + **P6 falsification gates** (`research/cci/{common,gate_guidance_return,gate_residual_alpha,gate_golden_discrimination}.py` — built+validated, **verdict DATA-GATED**) + **P7 cron** (`hermes-concalls.timer` Mon-Sat drain + `hermes-concalls-refresh.timer` Sun incremental, ≤18 Gemini/day). `/dash/concalls` + dossier + Pat all live. **The only thing left is DATA** — the 20/day Gemini free tier means the historical backfill accrues over ~2 weeks via the cron (or faster via claude.ai/paid Gemini); then re-run the gates = THE DECISION (standalone vs merge-into-pt14), then P8 backtest if they pass. Full design: `docs/concall-intelligence-design.md`; run-book §2d: `docs/concall-intelligence-NEXT-SESSION.md`. **UNCOMMITTED — commit gated on Ramana.**

### D59 — Concall guidance ledger: re-extraction wipes the WHOLE (symbol, source_period) set, settled rows included (2026-06-21)
`concall_extract._persist` deleted only `status='OPEN'` guidance before reinserting every statement as `OPEN`. Because the Phase-2 settlement pass (`concall_settle.py`) flips OPEN→MET/MISSED/PARTIAL, a `--force` re-extract (e.g. after a prompt/model bump) leaves the settled row behind AND inserts a fresh `OPEN` duplicate of the same promise → that statement is counted twice in `concall_guidance` → `guidance_accuracy_score` / `n_promises_resolved` in `concall_scores.py` corrupt. **Decision:** extraction OWNS a period's raw promise set; settlement is a deterministic, re-runnable derivation from later `concall_results`, so re-extraction deletes ALL rows for the `(symbol, source_period)` — settled included — matching the delete-set-then-reinsert idempotency the sibling concall tables already use; settlement is simply re-run afterwards (before `concall_scores --rerank`). No `UNIQUE(symbol, source_period, claim_text)` constraint: `claim_text` is an LLM paraphrase that drifts across prompt bumps (a content-hash key wouldn't catch the `--force` duplicate either), so the contract — not a row constraint — enforces single-copy. Bug is **live-reachable** (the settlement pass `concall_settle.py` IS built + committed `0d836dd`): it fires once extract→settle→`--force` re-extract hit the same period. Not yet triggered on real data (local DB has 0 guidance rows; VPS pilot still data-gated) → fixed pre-emptively. Settlement contract written into `docs/concall-intelligence-design.md` §5. Fix in `src/automation/concall_extract.py` (untracked/uncommitted with the rest of CCI Phase-0; commit gated on Ramana per design §11).

### D58 — SQLite `_tune`: `busy_timeout` MUST precede `journal_mode=WAL` (2026-06-21)
Pragma ORDER is load-bearing. A fresh connection starts at `busy_timeout=0`; flipping to WAL needs a brief exclusive lock, so `journal_mode`-first fails instantly with "database is locked" under any concurrency — this crashed the nightly `stock_rs` step on 2026-06-19 and left `hermes-bhavcopy.service` failed (the data was fine; it died at step 7 of 8). `busy_timeout` (raised 5s→30s) is now set first so the WAL flip waits out brief contention. **Do not reorder.** Committed `adaa443`; see `vps-deploy-reality` memory for the deploy/regression-watch note.

### D57 — Stock charts load FULL history; every chart names its scrip (2026-06-21)
The per-stock charts silently truncated to the most recent ~1300 trading rows (~5y), making "Max" start at ~2021 despite a 2004→ archive. Decision: charts show ALL available history ("Max" = max); the row cap is removed and the client-side range buttons still default the visible window. Reinforces the data-first principle ([[data-first-light-ui]]) — never display less data than exists. Companion: every chart self-identifies (ticker on every pane; ticker + company name on the price chart) — no unlabelled chart. Committed `7ece6df`.

### D56 — Explosive-move reverse-engineering: bottom-up strategy discovery + the validated "Launchpad" (2026-06-20)
Ramana asked for a from-scratch, data-driven discovery program (no given strategy): find genuine explosive movers, fingerprint the *pre-move* data state, mine recurring patterns, measure hit/success ratios. Built as an offline research layer (`research/explosive_moves/`, isolated `.venv-research`; production DB read-only). Full log + pattern library: **`docs/explosive-move-research.md`** (keep rich — binding doc-persistence rule).

**Method (rigor — see doc):** 3 rolling event studies — +10% day / +10% week / **Ramana's monthly = rolling +10% HELD over ~22td** (today ≥ +10% vs a month ago; *corrected from the initial wrong ≥20%-thrust-retain-50% bar — a genuine +10% that keeps all 10% must count*). Any-date rolling, never calendar-bucketed. Survivorship-safe (raw archive incl. delisted — 20–24% delisted/renamed); point-in-time ₹1cr liquidity; strictly as-of-base features; 1-in-10 reweighted quiet-day baseline; **OOS walk-forward both directions** + by-year + by-liquidity. ~149k events. **Raw price/volume/delivery is the PRIMARY discovery battery; DVPT/house = comparison ONLY** (Ramana: "don't lean on my strategy — show what the data finds"). **Rigor catch:** the v2 monthly onset-flip de-overlap created a base-day↔outcome coupling artifact (fake "ret_1d>0 ⇒ ~100% sustained") → caught + fixed with spacing-based de-overlap.

**Findings (hold OOS both directions + every year 2012–26):**
- **Moves are preceded by momentum + volatility + trend** (already rising, extended vs 20/50/200-DMA, off the 52w low, volatile; Cliff's δ up to +0.80) — NOT by a delivery surge.
- **★ Counter-DVPT (the headline answer to Ramana):** reading data ALONE, a *rising delivery footprint is NOT* what precedes moves — the winning rules prefer `deliv_qty_trend ≤ ~1.5` (no surge) + lower delivery%. DVPT's own RS-rank/accum-drift rank competitively-not-superior, are the house construct, and are sparse pre-2021. **The AI's independent read disagrees with the DVPT premise and holds OOS.** It *refines*, doesn't replace, the DVPT throughline (D47).
- **★ "Launchpad" (monthly +10% held, base 11%):** momentum-continuation (`ret_22d>7% AND vol not expanding AND ranging`, OOS TEST lift 7.1 / hit 80%) OR pullback-in-vol (`ret_22d≤7% AND vol_66>2.4% AND ret_1d≤−2.2%`, OOS 4.7). Combined **hit 63.5%, lift 5.7×**, +24%/66td, 80% win, **43% become ≥50% winners** (vs 3.7% base). Stronger in liquid names (>₹25cr: 86%; momentum-only **97%**). Holds every year.
- **Sustain = strength/control:** a +10% month HOLDS when launched from a calm/tight, non-falling, near-52w-high, closing-strong base (OOS **85%** vs 53.5% base) = Ramana's "genuine buying = the close holds."
- **NOT yet:** costs/slippage/sizing/entry-exit (precursor study, not a P&L backtest) → next builds.

### D55 — "Pat": a natural-language guided-search tab in the web tool (Gemini-only, glossary-grounded) — Phase 1 SHIPPED (2026-06-20)
Ramana asked for "an AI chatbot on my data, in plain English, in this tool" — named **Pat** (it's about *patterns*). Built as a tab in the web dashboard (**`/dash/pat`**), **NOT Telegram** (network-blocked), and **Gemini-Flash-only, never Claude** (his call; the cost-doctrine classifier path, ~13× cheaper than Haiku).

**WHY this shape:**
- **It generalizes the interface.** Instead of hand-building a command/panel per question, Pat answers ad-hoc questions over the existing data — the one feature that scales instead of adding to the pile.
- **"Train on our data" = GROUND, not fine-tune.** The asset is a hand-written **glossary** (`src/pat/glossary.py`) describing every metric/column/value in plain words; Pat reads it at question-time, live numbers always come fresh from the DB. Cheaper, always-current, and it powers both "explain a metric" and free-text understanding.
- **₹0 on the common path.** The guided **chips ARE the query parameters** → the tap-through path compiles to template SQL in pure Python (no LLM, can't hallucinate a column). Gemini Flash is used ONLY at the edges: free-text→params, and phrasing a glossary entry conversationally.

### D49h — Stock RS-overlay chart: gutter name labels replicated + the SAME boot-anchor drift fixed (found while replicating D49g) — FIXED (session 19)

While verifying hands-on I found the RS overlay had been **silently mis-anchoring all along** — contrary to the session-18 belief that it was the race-free "working reference." It rebased to a recent mid-window date (`2026-02-05`) instead of the full-series start (`2021-03-15`), so the lines didn't start at 100 on the left. SAME root cause as D49g, in two spots: (1) `reanchorToView()` read `getVisibleRange().from`, which lags a frame on first/off-screen layout (the overlay boots below the fold) → fixed by anchoring deterministically to `commonAnchor(null)` (the earliest point — valid because the overlay always `fitContent()`s the full series); (2) its `subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange` handler then re-anchored on settle/relayout events → fixed with the same `userInteracted` gate as D49g (pan-reanchor responds only to real user input). Verified live on RELIANCE: anchor holds at `2021-03-15` across boot + scroll (no drift), values reflect growth from 100 (RELIANCE 129.8 / Oil & Gas 159.3 / Nifty 500 174.8), all three gutter labels render and de-collide. ### D49g — /dash/compare chart: deterministic left-edge rebase + gutter name labels (the session-18 P0) — FIXED (session 19)

Both long-standing P0 compare-chart bugs shared ONE root cause: the chart's boot logic acted before lightweight-charts had laid out its first paint. Debugged hands-on in the live browser via the Chrome MCP — the prior blind `py_compile` + route-200 loop is exactly why it stayed unresolved across D49d/e/f.

- **Left-edge rebase.** `setRange()` correctly anchored each line to the window's deterministic left edge (`allT[len-n]`, e.g. 1Y → `2025-06-11`), but a layout-settling `subscribeVisibleTimeRangeChange` fired AFTER `internalSet` was cleared and re-anchored every line to a transient mid-window date (reproduced: `2026-02-05`), so the lines no longer started at 100 at the visible left edge. **Fix:** the fluid pan-to-reanchor now responds ONLY to genuine user interaction — a `userInteracted` flag, set by `wheel/pointerdown/mousedown/touchstart` listeners on the chart host, gates `scheduleRebase()`. Settle-time (non-user) range-change events are inert; range buttons and the pin still anchor explicitly. This is deterministic — it does NOT depend on settle timing, which is why D49d's `getVisibleRange()` read and D49e's `internalSet` seed both failed. The `rightOffset:3` and short-series-`commonAnchor` theories were the wrong layer.
- **Right-gutter name labels (built D49f).** Silently empty on load because `positionNames()` ran before the price scale existed, so `series.priceToCoordinate()` returned null and every label was skipped — with nothing re-triggering it until a pan/resize. **Fix:** a bounded `requestAnimationFrame` retry at boot re-runs `positionNames()` until each visible line's label is placed.

Verified live against real VPS data: a fresh load (zero interaction) holds the correct anchor AND renders names; all four ranges anchor to their own left edge (Max→`2021-06-02`, 3M→`2026-03-16`, 6M→`2025-12-11`, 1Y→`2025-06-11`); adding a short/newer 4th series (Nifty India Defence) does not corrupt the anchor and its label still renders. Deployed via `scp` + `systemctl restart hermes-api`. Follow-up (optional): replicate the `userInteracted` gate to the D48 stock RS-overlay chart if it ever shows the same boot drift (it currently uses `fitContent()`, which sidesteps the race).

### D46 — Bounded, prioritized batch pt14 scoring (B6) — lights up the Quality pillar, HONORS D8 — SHIPPED (session 18)
Building D45 exposed that the Quality pillar is dark: the Conviction shortlist (and the stock-page pt14 card, and the hub's "scored" count) read cached `pattern_scores`/`fundamentals`, which only exist for stocks someone has manually `/pt14`'d — so both D45 conviction names showed `unscored`. B6 fixes that by keeping the SURFACED names scored.

**The D8 tension, and how this honors it (NOT overturns it):** D8 is a deliberate "Ramana's call" — *"don't pre-scrape Screener for 5,000 stocks; wait for results events; cache 7 days; natural incremental growth."* A naive "score all ~2,400 equities nightly" would violate it. So `src/automation/score_batch.py` is explicitly the opposite of bulk:
- **Prioritized** — only the surfaced universe (watchlist → recent news-driven `screen_candidates` → Conviction shortlist → RS leaders), capped at 300, NOT the full equity list.
- **Incremental** — skips any symbol already scored within the 7-day TTL; each run only does outstanding work, so coverage grows over days then just refreshes ("natural incremental growth", D8's exact words).
- **Bounded** — at most `--limit` (default 40) real Screener scrapes per run; the rest wait for the next run.
- **Throttled** — a polite `--throttle` (default 2.5s) sleep after each real scrape (anti-rate-limit / anti-block). Fresh-cached names are re-scored locally with no network.
- **No LLM** — reuses the existing rule-based `scoring.score_symbol` (Screener HTML parse + `score_fundamentals`); ₹0 marginal.

D8 stays the doctrine; D46 is its careful application to the small set the system actually surfaces. Scheduled via a daily `hermes-pt14batch` systemd timer on the VPS (runs after the signals chain). Closes open item B6. The Conviction shortlist's ★ quality-confirmed dimension (and the stock-page pt14 card) now populate for surfaced names.

### D44 — Value-weighted institutional KEY PRICE + multi-horizon near-key entry + ticket/surge + one-screen workbench — SHIPPED (session 18)
Borrowed the genuinely-better ideas from an external "Delivery Per Order Screener" functional spec, implemented **strictly additively** (the non-regression mandate below was the user's hard requirement).

**Why (the flaw it fixes):** the D31 institutional zone `avg_close_p*` averages the **close** on the top-N power-DVPT days with **equal weight** (`sum(closes)/len`). But the biggest institutional day should DOMINATE the cost line, and the day's **avg_price** (not close) is where shares actually changed hands. So the flat zone can sit well away from where the size really transacted.

**What shipped (4 additive components, 15 new `stock_signals` columns):**
- **① Value-weighted key price** — `key_price_p{1m,2m,3m,6m,12m}` = Σ(price·w)/Σ(w) over the SAME top-N power-DVPT days `p_stats` already selects, where `price=avg_price` (fallback close) and `w=deliv_qty·price` (delivered value). The big day dominates; verified the value-weighting pulls the key BELOW the equal-weight avg when the biggest power day was the cheapest. **`avg_close_p*` left byte-identical** (kept for the reconciliation/history view).
- **② Asymmetric multi-horizon entry** — `gap_to_key_p{label}` = signed % of today's close vs each key (− below cost, + above). **near-key is DERIVED on read** (band `_KEY_BAND=(-1.0, 5.0)` — price at/just-above the institutional cost, not far below: close ∈ [key−1%, key+5%]). Independent of, and coexists with, the DVPT near-break (`next_p_above`/`gap_to_next_p_pct`).
- **③ Ticket size** — `avg_trade_qty` = volume/num_trades, `avg_deliv_qty_per_trade` = deliv_qty/num_trades (a cleaner direct ticket-size read than the D43 trade-count ratio).
- **④ Activity surge** — `turnover_surge_{1m,3m,1y}` = today value ÷ avg(value over the prior 30/90/360-cal-day window). A liquidity/attention filter complementary to DVPT.

**Non-regression mandate (honored):** every field is a NEW `_ensure_column`; the new compute is a SEPARATE block in the per-symbol pass that reuses the already-fetched window rows but alters no existing calc; a SEPARATE `--backfill-keyprice` (UPDATE-only on the 15 columns — never re-runs `--backfill-triggers`, which would needlessly rewrite established D28/D31/D43 values). Regression gate run on the VPS before shipping: snapshot existing columns for sample symbols, run the new backfill, assert existing columns unchanged (diff=0) and only the new columns populated.

**Store-raw/derive-flag (Doctrine C):** store the gaps; derive the near-key band on read so re-tuning `_KEY_BAND` needs no backfill. No LLM; value-based; calendar-day windows reuse `signals._WINDOWS`.

**Surfaced:** `/dash/stock` gets an "Institutional key price (value-weighted)" section beside the existing flat zones (key per horizon + signed gap + 🎯 launch-band read + ticket/surge); `/dash/stocks` gets a **🎯 Near key price** filter pill (existing screen + 🟢/🟡/🔴 marker unchanged) and a **Workbench ⇄** link; NEW **`/dash/workbench`** = the spec's "everything on one screen" — a wide read-only table (symbol · close · DVPT · rank · r/p · character · key_price_p* + gap_to_key_p* near-key-highlighted · power/avg_close ref · ticket · surge · total delivery ₹) reusing the existing `_DT_JS` toolbar (click-sort/filter/Export-CSV), `active="stocks"` (nav stays at 5 per D40-A). Telegram `/dvpt` gets a "📍 Key price (value-weighted)" block. Parked for later (open items): fiscal-quarter/week-number grain, query alerts, EWMA key-price variant.

### D43 — DVPT accumulation/distribution CHARACTER (Positioning pillar, item 1) — SHIPPED (session 18)
> Numbering note: the session kickstart called this "D42"; D42 was already taken by the equity-allowlist work (below), so this deepening of the Positioning signal is **D43**.

**The core principle — delivery data is SIDE-BLIND.** Every delivered share was simultaneously bought AND sold, so DVPT / delivery value / delivery % reveal the *size and ownership-intent of who transacted* — NEVER which side initiated. "High DVPT" means a strong hand was on **one** side of the tape; it does NOT say whether he was the buyer (accumulation) or the seller unloading into demand (distribution) — those wear nearly the same delivery signature. Only **price** reveals direction, and **trade-count breadth + trend location** separate strong-hand accumulation from strong-hands-distributing-to-retail. Hence **three independent axes — never collapsed into one number**:

| Axis | Answers | Stored fields |
|---|---|---|
| **WHO** | strong hands or retail crowd? | `deliv_value_ratio_1m_6m` (delivery ₹ picking up?), `trade_count_ratio_1m_6m` (≥1.3 broadening/retail · ≤1.1 concentrated/few-hands), `avg_deliv_pct_1m`/`_6m` |
| **WHICH WAY** | buyers or sellers initiating? | `deliv_updown_ratio_3m` (Σ delivery ₹ on up-days ÷ on down-days, 90d, on ADJUSTED closes), `accum_price_drift_3m` (the only direction-revealer) |
| **CONTEXT** | campaign vs one-off, where in the trend? | `pct_from_52w_high`, plus existing `p_score` persistence |

Key tell: **concentration** (high DVPT, contained trade count, price firm) = accumulating; **broadening** (rising trade count, falling avg ticket, high total delivery, price stalling near highs) = distributing into a retail crowd. Avg-ticket trend = `deliv_value_ratio ÷ trade_count_ratio` (derived on read, no column).

**Store the raw, derive the flag (Doctrine C).** The 7 numerics are stored; the `accum_character` label (TEXT) is DERIVED via `signals.accum_character(...)` so re-tuning thresholds needs no full backfill — `python -m src.automation.signals --relabel-character` re-derives every label in seconds. Default thresholds (TUNABLE, in `signals._CHAR_THRESH`; first match wins): `active`=p_score≥2 · `broadening`=tcr≥1.3 · `concentrated`=tcr≤1.1 · `up_skew`=updown≥1.30 · `down_skew`=updown≤0.77 · `price_up`=drift>5 · `price_down`=drift<−5 · `near_high`=pct_from_52w_high>−10. Rule: **DISTRIBUTION** if active AND (price_down OR (near_high AND not price_up)) AND (broadening OR down_skew); **ACCUMULATION** if active AND (price_up OR price_flat) AND (concentrated OR up_skew); **CONSOLIDATION** if (not active) AND price_flat; else **NEUTRAL**; NULL inputs → NULL ('-').

**Doctrine compliance:** no LLM (pure Python/SQL, nightly); value-based & split-invariant (delivery ₹ = deliv_qty × close); ADJUSTED closes (reuses `adjust.adjusted_closes`) for every direction/return read so a split can't fake a down-day; days with |daily return|>0.30 excluded as corp-action anomalies (D36 CC_THRESH); calendar-day windows (30/90/180) matching `signals._WINDOWS`.

**Shipped:**
- **`signals.py`** — shared label brain (`_char_flags` / `accum_character` / `accum_character_read`), metric compute (`_ret_signs` / `_character_metrics` / `_character_arrays`), folded into BOTH the live `compute_signals_for_symbol_date` (per-symbol fetch extended to 372 cal days for the 52w high; now also pulls `prev_close`+`deliv_per`) and the `--backfill-triggers` per-symbol pass (same batch UPDATE, +8 fields). New `--relabel-character` mode. ONE shared helper so dashboard + bot derive identical labels (DRY).
- **`db.py`** — 8 new `stock_signals` columns + `idx_signals_accum_character(trade_date, accum_character)`.
- **`dashboard.py`** — `_char_pill` + `.ca-*` pills; `/dash/stocks` daily gains a **Character** column, a **Total delivery ₹Cr** column, and **🟢 Accumulation / 🔴 Distribution** filter pills (wired into the existing `sflt` client filter via `data-accum`/`data-distrib`, composing with the `.dt` grid); weekly/monthly rollup carries the latest-day character; `/dash/stock` gets an **"Accumulation character"** panel (label + plain-English read + up/down delivery bar + WHO row + 52w-high distance + a ⚠️ distribution-while-high warning); Home gains a **"Stealth accumulation"** board (ACCUMULATION + p_score≥3 + concentrated + off-highs) and a Character pill on Top-trigger-stocks; `_PILLARS["POS"]` thesis now mentions character.
- **`telegram_bot.py`** — `/dvpt` gains a **🧭 Character** block; `/scan` + `/triggers` rows gain a **Ch** marker; `/triggers` gains modes **`accum`** (ACCUMULATION + p_score≥3 + concentrated) and **`distrib`** (DISTRIBUTION); `/start` help + `BOT_COMMANDS` updated. Same shared label helper as the dashboard.

**Verification:** all 4 modules `py_compile` clean; label rule + metric/anomaly-exclusion unit-tested synthetically (markup⇒ACCUMULATION, quiet base⇒ACCUMULATION/absorption, near-high broadening⇒DISTRIBUTION, split-day excluded from up/down skew, all boundaries); dashboard routes (`/dash`, `/dash/stocks` ±weekly/monthly, `/dash/stock`) return HTTP 200 on empty DB. Real-data eyeball + full backfill done on the VPS (see § Session log).

**Future (NOT built):** NSE **bulk & block deals** feed is the only source that names buyer/seller + side (trades >0.5% of equity) — the lone ground-truth for direction. Not ingested today; flagged in § "What's NOT yet built" as the next deepening of this pillar.

Convened a 5-perspective panel (quant/financial + equity-practitioner + data + UI/UX + architect). **Full design: `docs/rs-ratio-analysis-design.md`** (decisions D-A..D-H + phased tasks).

- **Phase B (one backfill):** smoothed/normalized ROC + cross-sectional z-momentum (2nd pass in `compute_for_date`) + volatility-scaled dead-band/hysteresis + a `/dash/rs` ranking page.
- Reuses the `/dash/stock` lightweight-charts block + existing `.p-*` palette. ⚠ Title-case index names (validate `idx` against `SELECT DISTINCT index_name`). No runtime LLM.

**Built (session 16, on-read — no schema change, no backfill):**

Deep-linked from RS cells. Guards size-index (no ratio_rows) + unknown-index.
