### Wolfe convergence rule — leg-ratio cap REPLACED by rail-crossing test (Ramana-directed, 2026-07-11) — LIVE
Ramana reasoned it from geometry (TIRUPATIFL — his manual draw the detector rejected): a wedge is valid iff its rails **1‑3 and 2‑4, extended, cross AFTER point 4** — a **slope** question (price ÷ time), not the price-only leg‑ratio the code used. The old `_classify` cap (`|leg34| ≤ |leg12|`) ignored time and wrongly killed converging wedges whose thrust leg 3‑4 out-priced leg 1‑2 (a slow, time-stretched leg 1‑2 parks point 2 late → steepens the 2‑4 rail into convergence — his exact insight).
- **FIX (`_classify`):** replaced the leg-ratio check with the crossing test — solve the bar where rails 1‑3 & 2‑4 meet, require it **> point‑4's bar**; parallel rails (no crossing) fail. **Direction-blind** — one formula, no bull/bear sign to flip (the trap he flagged). §A ordering/direction + the D108 fractal gate + §B + point-4 reconciliation all untouched. Tests added (`tests/test_wolfe.py`: converging-bear admitted · diverging-bear rejected · parallel rejected · converging-bull admitted).
- **Measured read-only on Nifty-500 before shipping:** 44,565 → 45,970 waves (net **+1,405**) — **admits ~4,551** true converging wedges the cap killed, **drops ~3,146** that passed on price-symmetry but whose rails never converge (false wedges). A correction both ways, not a loosening.
- **LIVE** (VPS scp of the union + writer-safe restart; `/dash` 200; backup `wolfe.py.bak-cross-20260712-081624`). Verified: TIRUPATIFL now admits his wave `1 Feb-18@44.9 · 2 Mar-2@37.2 · 3 Mar-19@58.7 · 4 Mar-23@47.5` (leg-ratio had rejected it). ### Wolfe point-4 reconciliation — detector picks the EXTREME point 4 (Ramana-directed, 2026-07-11) — LIVE (re-applied on top of the D111 §B rebalance)
Ramana flagged (TARSONS daily, Feb-2022) that point 4 was marked on a later, LOWER high (Feb-21 @ ₹674.5, a clean degree-5 Williams fractal) instead of the true apex (Feb-10 @ ₹698.8, degree-2). **ROOT CAUSE:** point 4 was UNDER-DEFINED — the code guards it FORWARD (`breached()`: no higher high pt4→pt5) but had NO BACKWARD guard, so among the multi-scale pivot union's competing point-4 candidates the §B score (which rewards fractal *cleanliness*) picked the tidier-but-lower high over the structural apex (point 4 = the max high (BULL) / min low (BEAR) in the pt3→pt5 window; only the forward half was enforced).
- **FIX:** new `wolfe._reconcile_point4()` — among waves sharing points 1-2-3, keep the one whose point 4 is the more extreme high/low ("select the maximum high before the next decline; exclude subsequent lower highs"). Applied at the SOURCE (`detect_waves` dedupe) so every surface (`overlay_for`/`winner_scan`/`/dash/wolfe`) inherits it; the display dedupe is untouched. **Orthogonal to the §B weightage incl. the same-day D111 rebalance** (a raw-price selection, not a score change) — re-applies as a clean +43-line additive hunk on top of `dfbe175`.
- **4-seat panel** (Wolfe-quant / charting-viz / skeptic-QA / Ramana-proxy) chose post-detection reconciliation **unanimously** over a detection-time backward guard, which they showed collapses into a wave-DROP: the true max-high candidate can fail the D108 fractal gate AND kill the lower fractal-valid twin → the wave vanishes (repeats the TCS silent-hide failure). Reconciliation only ever chooses among already-D108-gated candidates.
- **VERIFIED read-only on the live Nifty-500 archive:** 519 waves corrected / 284 symbols (1.2% of 45,083), **0 strictly-more-extreme violations**; winner-profile coverage intact (**822 → 822, 0 lost / 0 gained**; ~10 apex-date corrections); live scan changed by exactly **1 fresh row** (NATIONALUM BULL — apex corrected, geometry no longer clears the winner filter); TARSONS overlay → `('BULL','2022-02-10',698.8)`. Regression test `tests/test_wolfe.py` (4 tests; none existed for wolfe.py before).
- **⚠ FLIP INCIDENT (multi-session, recorded as a lesson):** the first deploy (baseline `e6c75d6` + point-4) went live + verified, but a parallel session's **D111 §B-rebalance deploy full-scp'd `wolfe.py` and reverted the point-4 fix on the VPS**. Reconciled: point-4 re-applied ON TOP of the §B rebalance on **main** (this commit carries BOTH), then redeployed. **`wolfe.py` deploys must henceforth ship main's current file (§B + point-4) — never a stale copy.** §A geometry + §B math + the D108 gate all untouched. Commit «P4-HASH».

### Session 83i — 2026-07-08 — Pat eval gate: 6 pre-existing misses fixed → battery 100% green + strict-by-default + nightly pager (AUD-40 follow-through)
AUD-40 wired the Pat NL eval battery into a gate (`src/pat/eval_set.py --gate` + gate-0.5 in
`scripts/regression_sweep.sh`) but it ran WARN-only against a known ~6-miss baseline. This session
cleared the baseline (root-caused + fixed every one), made the gate environment-independent, flipped
it to strict, and added a nightly enforcing timer. **Committed to `main` (paths below); Pat src files
scp'd to the VPS + gate re-run there = 100% green on live data (ROUTE 64/64 · EXPLAIN 558/558 ·
COMPILER 31/31 · HALLUCINATION 8/8 · ACCURACY 10/10).**
- **The 6 misses — diagnosed, not silenced:**
  1. **ROUTE `cheap stocks under PE 15` → `val:''` (wanted `deep`).** The compiler already maps a
     `{valuation,<,15}` filter to the deep tier (its INTENT case passed) — but `parse_fallback`
     never *extracted* "under PE 15" into a filter, so the ₹0 degraded path emitted bare
     `metric:valuation` → default cheap. **Fix:** new `detect_pe_threshold()` (both orderings:
     "under PE 15" / "PE over 80") in `understand.py`, wired into `_parse_fallback_inner` → emits the
     valuation filter (and sets `metric=valuation` when otherwise unset).
  2–3. **EXPLAIN `explain vs market` / `explain vs sector` → None.** `detect_compare`'s `_VS_RE`
     read "explain vs market" as compare(EXPLAIN, MARKET), stealing it before the explain path (the
     `what is…`/`what does…` templates already passed — only `explain X` collided). **Fix:** expanded
     `detect_compare`'s stop-set with explain-lead words (EXPLAIN/DEFINE/WHAT/…) + non-ticker RHS
     words (MARKET/SECTOR/NIFTY/INDEX/BROAD/PEERS).
  4–6. **EXPLAIN `financials & the pt14 score — a known limitation` → None.** The only glossary term
     >45 chars whose long part is NOT parenthetical (the eval strips parens, so the other 4 long
     terms pass) — so `parse_fallback`'s `len(term)<=45` guard returned None before it could resolve.
     **Fix:** renamed the term to the real term **`Financials & the pt14 score`** (the "known
     limitation" caveat already lives in `plain`/`detail`); slug `financials_adaptation` unchanged →
     zero external-ref breakage.
- **Gate hardened (so strict-by-default is correct EVERYWHERE, not just where a file is absent):**
  (a) the **CATALOG** eval is now PRINTED but NOT gated — it's a deterministic-FLOOR *coverage*
  metric (141/202; many phrasings legitimately return None and defer to the live model), and it only
  ever "passed" on the VPS because `docs/pat-question-catalog.md` is absent there; gating a by-design
  <100% metric would wedge the gate on any dev checkout. Matches gate-0.5's stated battery
  (compiler·route·explain·hallucination·accuracy). (b) the **ACCURACY** eval now treats a missing
  table/column as a SKIP, not a FAIL — a feature's schema absent in THIS env (e.g. a partial dev DB
  lacking `stock_oscillators`) can't be tested; a predicate violation is still the real signal.
- **Enforcement:** `regression_sweep.sh` gate-0.5 flipped to **strict by default**
  (`PATEVAL_STRICT` default 0→1; `PATEVAL_STRICT=0` remains a documented WARN-only escape hatch).
  NEW nightly **`hermes-pateval.{service,timer}`** (08:15 UTC daily, `--gate`) +
  `95-onfailure.conf` → `OnFailure=hermes-alert@%n` = the AUD-26 Telegram-DM pager (which HAS
  landed — DM proven live 2026-07-07). Installed on the VPS, `daemon-reload`, manual service run =
  green (Result=success), timer enabled + scheduled; units version-controlled in
  `scripts/systemd/vps-live/`.
- **NOT restarted:** hermes-api left running — a research writer (`explosive_moves.dividend_drift
  --run`) held the DB at wrap (DB-lock-restart hazard). The gate/timer import the new files fresh
  from disk (green now); live Pat picks up the minor `understand.py`/`glossary.py` changes on its
  next natural restart (fallback-path + one compare edge case + a glossary label — no live regression).
- **Paths:** `src/pat/understand.py` · `src/pat/glossary.py` · `src/pat/eval_set.py` ·
  `scripts/regression_sweep.sh` · `scripts/systemd/vps-live/hermes-pateval.{service,timer}` +
  `hermes-pateval.service.d/95-onfailure.conf`.

Follow-ons to the Session-62 rotation/band **timeline scrubber** (all on `main`, deployed + browser-verified):
- **Clock parity** (`9b22882`): the `/dash/rsband?view=clock` dial got the same draggable scrubber + month badge (reuses `band_path` + `pibAt` interpolation; "Breathe" retained + synced) — so toggling Lanes↔Clock no longer loses the control. Consistency map: scrubber is on ALL multi-sector maps (RRG `/dash/rrg` + embed, band Lanes, Constituents drill-down, Clock) via the shared `_sectors_rrg_block` / `_chart_block`; single-sector Channel views are intentionally left (they're already interactive time-series charts).
- **Scrub trail de-cluttered** (`0006033` → `0a2d278`): manual scrub had drawn every sector's FULL journey to the cursor → ~19 overlapping paths buried the dots. Now a faint ~3-point heading stub only. Play's rolling comet unchanged.
- **Hover-to-trace while scrubbed + richer readouts** (`eed0b4f`): a parked/scrubbed RRG frame is now hoverable (global `HK` = journey-head fraction) — hover a sector to trace its journey UP TO that month with a month-aware tooltip (quadrant + RS-ratio/mom AT the cursor). Channel hover tooltip now names the zone (cheap/mid/rich).
- **Doctrine (Ramana):** the single intent of the pattern-identification project is *maximum understanding from a minimal, clean set of interactive charts* — every element must earn its place. Apply to all future viz work.
- **Linked time-cursor (`61c387e`), first application of the doctrine:** on the single-**sector** band page (`/dash/rsband?idx=`) a compact date-tagged RS-Ratio×RS-Momentum **rotation tail** now sits under the channel; ONE shared cursor ties them by date — hover the channel → the same moment lights on the tail (`window.__tailMark`), hover a tail dot → the channel crosshair jumps to that date (`window.__chGoto`). Read **level (band) ↔ rotation (quadrant) at the same instant**. Design rationale: scrubbing is a *map* idiom (time hidden → replay); a single name is a *time-series* (time on x) → the right interaction is a **linked readout**, not another scrubber. Stocks keep channel-only (no sector RRG tail). Deferred single-sector-RRG scrubber (my earlier proposal) intentionally NOT built — the linked cursor is the analyst-preferred alternative.
- Method: all edits done in **isolated git worktrees** (shared tree flips under parallel colour sessions) → validated scratch artifacts (compile + render smoke-test) → scp deploy → commit → push. New-gen `rsband.py` is committed (`1fd8c19`) so `main→VPS` can't re-500 `/dash`.

Ramana spotted the Tracker workspace rendering **two identical sub-nav strips** (registry text-links + legacy `_track_subnav` pills) and — rightly — asked how a UI-focused process missed it, and whether *tabs were also missing*. Both turned out to be the same root cause: nothing forced the nav graph to agree with the route table.
- **Root cause (a refactor seam):** Tracker was historically the ONE workspace special-cased to draw its own in-page strip (`_track_subnav`, called from page bodies) instead of the shell's `_SUBNAV`. The Nav-IA pass (`d15a60d`) then generalized sub-nav rendering to the registry for *every* altitude (incl. Tracker) and neutralized the one legacy hook it knew about (`_subnav`) — but `_track_subnav` is a SECOND, bespoke function it didn't know to silence. So the generalization double-rendered exactly the workspace that was special-cased.

### Session 57 — 2026-06-30 — CCI same-unit SEMANTIC mismatches (the residual `0e8e8b7` left) — commit `<pending>`
The mixed-UNIT walkback bug was fixed in `0e8e8b7` (Session 56's CCI pass). That fix flagged a **residual** for review: same-unit *semantic* mismatches that still emit wrong credibility signals. This session closes the two confirmed residual classes in `concall_diff.py` (the deterministic deterioration diff that **drives the credibility rank** via `concall_scores` `_DETERMINISTIC_FLAGS` / `DETER_PEN_PER`). Built ON `0e8e8b7` (kept `_unit_family`/`_implausible_money`/UNSETTLEABLE); did not revert it. Owned files only: `concall_diff.py` (the other two — `concall_settle.py`, `concall_extract.py` — needed no change; the settle scale-gate from `0e8e8b7` already covers the segment-vs-consolidated settle case, and the subject guard reads the existing `claim_text`, so no schema/subject column was added).
- **Residual 1 — SUBJECT/REFERENT walkback (same unit, different thing).** `guidance_walkback` bucketed by (statement_type, unit_family) and `max()`-ed the pool — so it compared CGPOWER's *industrial-systems full-year growth 14-15%* (Aug 2018) against *"the Indonesia JV will add ~150 bps to margins"* (Feb 2019, stored 1.5%) and fabricated **"revenue lowered 15→1.5"**. Same unit (%), different referent. **Fix:** new `_subject_mismatch(prev_claims, cur_claims)` — when a SPECIFICALLY NAMED sub-entity (JV / subsidiary / named geography / brand / intercompany line, vocab `_SUBENTITY_CUES` + scope words `standalone`/`consolidated`) appears in the `claim_text` of exactly ONE of the two compared periods (the referent shifted between a part and the whole), the targets are not-comparable → suppress, never emit a Δ. Tight by design (referent-defining tokens only, NOT generic words like `bps`/`each`/`per ton`), so a real same-subject lowering is untouched; the same entity on BOTH sides (a genuine JV walkback) is NOT suppressed.
- **Residual 2 — COVERAGE-GAP drop.** `promise_quietly_dropped` fired across multi-year gaps (CGPOWER *"capex from Feb 2019 not reaffirmed in Jul 2025"* = a 77-month NCLT/insolvency-era blackout) — but a promise can't be "walked back" if there was simply no concall in between. **Fix:** new named constant **`MAX_REAFFIRM_GAP_MONTHS = 24`** + `_gap_months()`; suppress the drop when prev→cur straddles a gap > 24mo. Chosen from the live ledger (sharply bimodal: p90 of all P→Q gaps = 6mo; clean break to 127 flags at >24mo; the 22–24mo bucket is EMPTY → 24 is a true distribution gap). Leaves the 13–21mo COVID-era single-misses alone (a 1–2yr non-reaffirmation can still be real).
- **Verify (VPS real data, NO LLM — `concall_diff` is pure-deterministic).** Re-ran `concall_diff --all` then `concall_scores --rerank`. SQL before/after: `guidance_walkback` **896 → 799** (97 suppressed); `promise_quietly_dropped` **2,391 → 2,264** (127 suppressed). ### Session 56 — 2026-06-29 — P0: the impossible "representative receipt" on Coverage (provenance integrity)
[P0] The QA Round-2 register (`docs/QA-round2-register.md`, top-5 #1) caught the lead trust wedge on `/dash/coverage` surfacing a **logically impossible** filing date: the "Representative conservative" receipt showed FINPIPE Q `2024-12-31` filed `2024-01-18` — ~11 months *before* the quarter even ended. Fixed end-to-end on the VPS.
- **Root cause = a clerical YEAR-TYPO in the BSE source subject, parsed literally.** The 15 corrupt rows in `provenance_knowable` were ALL Dec-31 quarters where the company's own BSE result announcement carried the wrong year in its headline — e.g. FINPIPE filed 2024-01-18 with subject *"...Quarter And Nine Months Ended 31St December, **2024**"* (should be Dec-**2023**); IDEA filed 2023-02-14 says "31 December **2023**" (Dec-2022); CONFIPET filed 2025-02-08 says "December 31, **2025**" (Dec-2024). `period_from_subject` faithfully parsed the typo'd year → a period_end ~320–348 days AFTER the filing date, and the correct year-1 quarter was never captured. NOT a fiscal-vs-calendar bug in our derivation; the parser was correct, the *source* was wrong, and we had no structural guard against an impossible (real < period_end) pairing.
- **Fix 1 — derivation invariant (`fundamentals_filing_dates.py`).** New `_decorrupt_period_end(period_end, filing_date)`: a results filing can never predate its period, so when a headline-parsed period_end is *after* the filing date, walk the YEAR back (month/day preserved → quarter identity unchanged) to the nearest occurrence ≤ filing date. Wired into `choose_periods` before the candidate intersection; plus a HARD write-guard in `match_announcements` that drops any `period_end > filing_date` pairing regardless of derivation path. (So FINPIPE's typo'd announcement now correctly binds to `2023-12-31`.)
- **Fix 2 — picker guard (`provenance.py:lag_samples`).** Defensive: skip any captured row where `real < period_end` before building the `leaks`/`conservative` receipt lists, so even a surviving corrupt row can never be selected as the headline proof in `provenance_narrative()` / the Coverage wedge.
- **Data cleanup (VPS).** Backed up all rows for the 15 symbols (`data/backups/provenance_15syms_pre-fix_*.tsv`), deleted the 15 corrupt rows, and re-ran the FIXED `backfill_symbol` for those symbols → the 8 whose corrected Dec quarter is in the archive re-captured with the right period_end (the other 7 correctly captured nothing — that Dec-year-1 quarter isn't in `fundamentals_history`). **SQL audit: corrupt rows (real < period_end) = 15 → 0** (whole table). Refreshed `provenance_lag_calibration` (unchanged chosen lags A=114/Q=59 — the corrupt rows were always clipped out, so calibration was never poisoned).
- **Verify (VPS live).** `provenance_narrative()` now leads with **conservative = SWSOLAR 2022-03-31 A: modelled 2022-06-29 vs real 2022-04-07 (-83d)** (filed 8d after FY-end — plausible & honest) and **worst = ATLASCYCLE 2021-06-30 Q: real 2023-06-09 (+659d)** (a genuine late-filer leak case). `lag_samples` returns **0 impossible receipts**. ### Session 51 — 2026-06-29 — Release gate upgraded: a CLEAN-CHECKOUT chrome contract gate (D74)
[P0] The release gate only proved the live VPS *answered* every route with a 200. But the v2 chrome is wired at runtime by `v2_surfaces.wire()` and every hook is **defensive** (a failure is logged + swallowed so a page never 500s) — so the site could silently revert to the legacy chrome (green-"e" logo, old search box, flat top bar) while every route still returned 200, and the live-200 sweep would call it a PASS. Closed that gap with an in-process chrome gate that asserts WHAT was served, not just that *something* was.
- **`scripts/chrome_gate.py`** (NEW) — builds the app **in-process from the current checkout** via `TestClient` (no network, no live VPS), reproduces production wiring (`v2_surfaces.wire`, applied idempotently — also independent of whether `main.py` already holds the D73 hook), renders the real pages and asserts the chrome markers: **`uk-skin`** (shell_skin reskin applied), **`v2bar`** (canonical 4-altitude nav), **`Trust`** (Coverage utility), **`Wire`** (`/dash/wire` mounted + linked), and **NO `class="hsearch"`** (legacy search form swapped out). Two page classes: 10 **legacy** `_shell` pages (must carry all 5 markers) + 4 **native** ui_kit pages (coverage/screen2/strategist/_ui — own chrome, asserted 200 + Trust + Wire only). The `.hsearch` marker checks the element `class="hsearch"`, NOT the substring — `hsearch` also appears in the skin's CSS rule (`.hsearch input`), which would false-positive.
- **`scripts/regression_sweep.sh`** — now a **two-gate** harness: Gate 1 = the chrome gate (runs locally/in-process, regardless of `HOST`); Gate 2 = the existing live-200 + overlay sweep. Picks the first python that can `import fastapi` (repo `.venv` first, VPS-style); skips-with-loud-warning (not a hard fail) if no such interpreter exists so a deps-less shell still runs the live sweep. `SKIP_CHROME=1` opts out.
- **Verify (local, this laptop):** `python scripts/chrome_gate.py` → **PASS** (10 legacy + 4 native, all markers present); non-vacuous proven — synthetic reverted-chrome HTML (no skin/nav/Trust/Wire + leaked `.hsearch`) yields **5** correctly-labelled failures incl. the "leaked" `.hsearch`, and a 500 is caught. `bash -n` clean; both new files **LF** (VPS-safe). `regression_sweep.sh` Gate 1 runs + passes; Gate 2 (live VPS) unchanged. Files: `scripts/chrome_gate.py` (new), `scripts/regression_sweep.sh`, this PROJECT_STATE update. Builds on D73 ([[lane-a2-native-ui-design-system]]).

**Nightly DB-lock fix — `src/core/db.py` `_tune` (commit `adaa443`):**
- `hermes-bhavcopy.service` had been `failed` since 2026-06-19. Diagnosis: the **data was fine** (bhav/signals/indexes/index_signals/membership/equity_list/RS/CPR all reached 06-19); the chain crashed at step 7 of 8 (`stock_rs`) with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked` at `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`. **Root cause:** `_tune` ran `journal_mode=WAL` BEFORE setting `busy_timeout`; a fresh connection defaults to `busy_timeout=0`, and the WAL flip needs a brief exclusive lock, so under concurrency (heavy manual VPS dev that day) it failed instantly instead of waiting. **Fix:** set `busy_timeout=30000` FIRST, then `journal_mode=WAL` (D58).
- Applied surgically on the VPS (backup `db.py.bak.lockfix-20260621-173141`), cleared the failed flag (`systemctl reset-failed`), restarted `hermes-api` + `hermes-telegram` so all services pick it up, and landed in git isolated from the in-flight CCI `db.py` WIP via plumbing (`git hash-object` + `update-index --cacheinfo`). **Verified post-fix by re-running the failed `stock_rs` step** under the patched db.py — clean through all 2415 per-symbol connections ("computed 2415 RS rows, 1364 ranked for 2026-06-19"). The Mon 2026-06-22 14:00 UTC scheduled run is the production confirmation.

### Session 25 — 2026-06-20 — Explosive-move reverse-engineering research program — v3 COMPLETE, corrected per Ramana (offline, not deployed)
**Context:** Ramana: "I am not going to give you strategy… I want you to find strategy… ground-breaking. Identify stocks that moved 10% in a month and sustained, 10% in a week, 10% in a day; track back; identify the data patterns; compile them; understand the hit ratio and success ratio." A from-scratch, bottom-up discovery program. (Decision **D56**.)
**Built — new offline research layer `research/explosive_moves/` (isolated `/opt/hermes/.venv-research`; production `hermes.db` READ-ONLY; outputs → `/opt/hermes/data/research.db` + `out/*.csv`):**
- `common.py` (read-only DB, reused `adjust.py` standalone, per-symbol numpy series + point-in-time trailing-median turnover, Cliff's δ), `events.py` (3 detectors + forward outcomes), `features.py` (precursor matrix: raw descriptors + house `stock_signals` + CPR, as-of-t-1, 1-in-10 reweighted baseline), `mine.py` (univariate lift/precision/coverage + depth-3 CART rules + RF importance), `validate.py` (walk-forward OOS both directions + success ratio), `sensitivity.py` (liquidity + by-year robustness), `run_all.py` (orchestrator).
- **Corpus (v3):** 2012→2026, **~149k events** (13,720 daily / 52,791 weekly / 69,746 monthly +10%-intramonth, **37,343 sustained = 53.5%**) vs ~29.9k reweighted baseline. Survivorship-safe (20–24% delisted/renamed).
- **⚠ CORRECTED per Ramana (v2/v3):** (1) monthly = **rolling +10% HELD** over ~22td, NOT the initial ≥20%-thrust-retain-50% (a genuine +10% that keeps all 10% must count); (2) **rolling, any-date** (not calendar); (3) **raw data is the PRIMARY discovery battery, DVPT = comparison ONLY** ("don't lean on my strategy"); (4) expanded the raw delivery/volume battery; (5) **caught + fixed a base-day↔outcome coupling artifact** in the v2 monthly onset-flip (→ spacing-based de-overlap).
**Result (raw-only, validated OOS both directions + every year 2012–26):** **★ Counter-DVPT headline** — reading data alone, a *delivery surge is NOT what precedes moves* (winning rules want `deliv_qty_trend ≤ ~1.5`, lower delivery%); momentum+volatility+trend lead (δ up to +0.80); DVPT RS/accum-drift are competitive-not-superior + the house's own. The **"Launchpad"** (momentum-continuation `ret_22d>7% AND vol-not-expanding AND ranging` OOS lift 7.1/hit 80%; OR pullback-in-vol `ret_22d≤7% AND vol_66>2.4% AND ret_1d≤−2.2%` OOS 4.7) → combined **hit 63.5%, lift 5.7×**, +24%/66td, 80% win, 43% become ≥50% winners (vs 3.7% base); stronger in liquid names (>₹25cr 86%, momentum-only 97%). Sustain = strength/control (calm/tight, non-falling, near-52w-high base → OOS 85% vs 53.5%) = "genuine buying." Refines, doesn't replace, the DVPT throughline (D47).
**Deliverable:** `docs/explosive-move-research.md` (methodology + ranked precursor catalog + the Pattern Library cards M1/M2/W1/D1/S1 + caveats + reproduce steps). **NOT committed/deployed** (offline research; awaiting Ramana's call to turn the Launchpad into a live screener). No production code touched. **Commit:** _(pending — ask before committing)_.

### Session 18 (continued) — 2026-06-18 — D44 value-weighted key price + multi-horizon entry + workbench (additive)
Borrowed the genuinely-useful ideas from an external "Delivery Per Order Screener" spec and shipped them **strictly additively** (the user's hard non-regression requirement). The fix: D31's flat `avg_close_p*` zone equal-weights *close* on the top-N power days, so the BIG institutional day doesn't dominate the cost line and the day's *avg_price* (where shares actually traded) is ignored. D44 adds, without touching any existing column: ① **value-weighted `key_price_p*`** (Σ price·deliv-value ÷ Σ deliv-value over the same top-N power days, priced at avg_price); ② **`gap_to_key_p*`** + an asymmetric **near-key** band derived on read (`_KEY_BAND=(-1,+5)` — price at/just-above institutional cost); ③ **ticket size** (avg_trade_qty, avg_deliv_qty_per_trade); ④ **turnover surge** (1m/3m/1y). 15 new `stock_signals` columns.

Approach (non-regression): a SEPARATE compute block in the per-symbol pass reusing the already-fetched window rows (zero change to D28/D31/D43 paths); a SEPARATE `--backfill-keyprice` that UPDATEs ONLY the 15 columns (never re-runs `--backfill-triggers`). Surfaced: `/dash/stock` key-price section beside the flat zones; `/dash/stocks` 🎯 near-key pill + Workbench link (existing screen/markers unchanged); NEW `/dash/workbench` (wide sortable/exportable table reusing `_DT_JS`); `/dvpt` 📍 key-price block. Parked (open items B8): fiscal-quarter/week grain (+ the `docs/multi-timeframe-positioning-design.md` D42/D43 renumber note), saved-query alerts, EWMA key-price.

Verification: 4 modules `py_compile` clean; synthetic unit test PASSES the value-weighting spot-check (biggest power day cheapest ⇒ key 82.95 vs equal-weight 117.0) + asymmetric band + ticket/surge; dashboard routes (incl. `/dash/workbench`) HTTP 200.

**Shipped & deployed:** code commit **`d6195c3`** (pushed to `main`); FF-pulled on the VPS, `hermes-api` restarted (active). **Regression gate PASSED (ship-blocker)** — snapshot of 5 symbols before/after `--backfill-keyprice`: **73 existing columns byte-identical**, 15 new columns added, 6,250 rows populated. Full `--backfill-keyprice`: **3,053 symbols / 2,384,778 rows (~7 min** — lighter than D43 since no adjusted-close build). Real-data spot-check (2026-06-17, 2,427 rows; key_price_p3m on 100%, 1,161 near-key): ① value-weighting demonstrably repositions the cost line vs the equal-weight `avg_close_p12m` in BOTH directions — AQYLON key 142.1 vs avgclose 301.4 (−52.8%, its biggest power day far cheaper), MCX −29.2%, vs SILVERTUC/COCKERILL +30–60% (big day expensive); ② near-key gaps all within [−1%,+5%] (ASHOKLEY +0.7%, CCL −0.0%, FINPIPE +4.0%); ③ ticket size sane (deliv/trade ≤ trade qty always); ④ surge discriminating (0.4×–55×). **All spec verification steps satisfied.** (Known carry-over: key/avg_close zones use raw close → a split inside the window shows a pre-split key, e.g. SILVERTUC close 195 vs key 1137 — the SAME property the existing D31 zones have; addressed by open item B5 zones-on-adjusted-price, not a D44 regression.)

### Session 18 — 2026-06-18 — D43 DVPT accumulation/distribution CHARACTER (Positioning pillar, item 1)
Deepened the Positioning signal with the one thing the R/P trigger system structurally cannot tell you: delivery data is **side-blind** (every delivered share was simultaneously bought AND sold), so a high p_score is equally consistent with a strong hand *accumulating* and a strong hand *distributing into a retail bid*. Built a 3-axis read — **WHO** (trade-count breadth + delivery-₹ trend + delivery %), **WHICH WAY** (adjusted-price drift + value-weighted up/down delivery skew — price is the only direction-revealer), **CONTEXT** (52w-high distance + p_score persistence) — into 7 stored numerics + a derived `accum_character` label (ACCUMULATION/DISTRIBUTION/CONSOLIDATION/NEUTRAL). Store-the-raw/derive-the-flag (Doctrine C): thresholds are tunable and re-derivable via `--relabel-character` with no measure recompute. Scope-disciplined to this ONE pillar item; RS + Quality untouched.

Shipped (decision **D43**; kickstart called it "D42" but that number was taken by the equity-allowlist work, so it's D43):

- **⚠ HONEST FINDING, fenced in the docstring (matters for whoever builds the surface): HUB COUNTERPARTS ARE NOT INSIGHT.** 7 rating agencies cover 63+ companies each → an agency co-link is structurally guaranteed and says NOTHING about the pair; "connected to 74 companies!" would be an artefact of CARE Ratings existing. The INFORMATIVE co-links are the sparse ones: shared insider (67 filers touch >1 company) · acquirer (111) · deal counterparty (97) · lender (46). A surface must rank by counterpart SCARCITY and never headline a raw degree count. **Degree is not importance** — and a degree turned into a score needs its own prereg.
- **Feed-depth corroboration (unplanned):** the live insider edges span only **2025-11-01..2026-07-14** (~8 months) — which independently confirms the premise of the E-03 block (feed too shallow for clustered inference, t_cohort NaN). The fence is not theoretical; the data says the same thing.
